title: Dynamic Logistics Routing Engine
business: Global logistics firms managing complex, multi-modal freight delivery networks.
problem: Hard-coded routing logic creates rigid systems where adding new carrier-specific calculation methods requires modifying core business logic, leading to high regression risks and deployment bottlenecks.
solution: The Strategy Pattern encapsulates interchangeable routing algorithms behind a common interface, allowing the system to swap calculation logic at runtime without altering the client code that requests the route.
steps: Define a common RoutingStrategy interface with an execute method.
Implement concrete classes for specific algorithms like AirFreight, SeaFreight, and GroundTransport.
Configure a context object to hold a reference to a RoutingStrategy implementation.
Inject the required strategy into the context based on user-selected criteria.
Execute the strategy through the context interface to retrieve the calculated route.
outcome: Improved system maintainability and modularity, enabling developers to introduce new routing algorithms as independent components without risking the stability of existing delivery logic.
limitation: The primary limitation is the increased complexity caused by the proliferation of strategy classes; developers must monitor the number of objects created to ensure the system remains navigable and check for redundant logic by reviewing the strategy interface implementation count.
